items.informal_name: Second factor in the universal factorization of a monic polynomial of degree n into degrees m and k
items.type:
{R : Type u_1} →
  [inst : CommRing R] →
    {n : ℕ} →
      (m k : ℕ) →
        (hn : n = m + k) →
          (p : Polynomial.MonicDegreeEq R n) →
            Polynomial.MonicDegreeEq (Polynomial.UniversalFactorizationRing m k hn p) k
items.informal_description: The monic polynomial of degree $ k $ obtained as the second factor in the universal factorization of a monic polynomial $ p $ of degree $ n = m + k $, constructed via the canonical equivalence between $ R $-algebra homomorphisms and polynomial factorizations. This factor corresponds to the image of the universal factorization map applied to the tensor product decomposition $ R[\Fin m] \otimes_R R[\Fin k] $.

items.informal_name: Multivariate Polynomial Rings are Unique Factorization Monoids
items.type:
∀ (σ : Type v) {D : Type u} [inst : CommRing D] [UniqueFactorizationMonoid D],
  UniqueFactorizationMonoid (MvPolynomial σ D)
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $D$ and type $\sigma$, the multivariate polynomial ring $D[\sigma]$ is a unique factorization monoid. This means that every non-zero, non-unit polynomial in $D[\sigma]$ can be factored uniquely into irreducible polynomials, up to order and multiplication by units.

items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : CommRing R] → {n : ℕ} → (m k : ℕ) → n = m + k → Polynomial.MonicDegreeEq R n → Type u_1
items.informal_description: The ring obtained by localizing the universal factorization ring presentation with respect to the Jacobian determinant of the presentation, ensuring invertibility of the Jacobian to facilitate coprime factorizations of monic polynomials of degree $n = m + k$ over a commutative ring $R$.

items.informal_name: Product of First and Second Factors in Universal Factorization of Monic Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {n : ℕ} (m k : ℕ) (hn : n = m + k) (p : Polynomial.MonicDegreeEq R n),
  ↑(Polynomial.UniversalFactorizationRing.factor₁ m k hn p) *
      ↑(Polynomial.UniversalFactorizationRing.factor₂ m k hn p) =
    ↑(Polynomial.UniversalFactorizationRing.monicDegreeEq m k hn p)
items.informal_description: In the universal factorization ring for monic polynomials of degree $ n = m + k $, the product of the first factor (of degree $ m $) and the second factor (of degree $ k $) equals the monic polynomial of degree $ n $, i.e., $ \text{factor}_1 \cdot \text{factor}_2 = p $.

items.informal_name: Second factor in the universal coprime factorization of a monic polynomial of degree n into degrees m and k
items.type:
{R : Type u_1} →
  [inst : CommRing R] →
    {n : ℕ} →
      (m k : ℕ) →
        (hn : n = m + k) →
          (p : Polynomial.MonicDegreeEq R n) →
            Polynomial.MonicDegreeEq (Polynomial.UniversalCoprimeFactorizationRing m k hn p) k
items.informal_description: The monic polynomial of degree $k$ obtained as the second factor in the universal coprime factorization of a monic polynomial $p$ of degree $n = m + k$, constructed by applying the canonical algebra homomorphism from the universal factorization ring to the universal coprime factorization ring. This factor corresponds to the image of the universal factorization map under localization with respect to the Jacobian determinant, ensuring coprimality of the factors.
